title: Underived open-composition and restriction models respect counits
statement: Let $h:X\to Y$ be a scheme morphism [def-pc-scheme], $U\subseteq Y$ an arbitrary open, $V=h^{-1}U$, $g:V\to U$ and $j_X,j_Y$ the open inclusions. On homotopy categories of module complexes let $\alpha_0:h_*r_Y\cong r_Xg_*$ and $\beta_0:j_{X*}h_*\cong g_*j_{Y*}$ be the fixed models [def-pc-derived-mayer-vietoris-open-counit-model], with open adjunction counits $\varepsilon_X,\varepsilon_Y$ [def-pc-kinjective-mayer-vietoris-data]. For every homotopy object K on V, $r_Y(\beta_{0,K});\varepsilon_{Y,g_*K}=\alpha_{0,j_{X*}K};g_*(\varepsilon_{X,K})$. This is an underived sectionwise identity: no derived category, derived comparison or derived adjunction is involved.

source.place: Tags 08FE, 0D5T and 08BV; official pages https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08FE, https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0D5T and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08BV, read 2026-10-14

proof.text:
on an open W of U, both composites are the restriction identification of
sections of I over g inverse image W. Use restrictAdjunction_counit_app_app for
the two counits and the sectionwise formulas for pushforwardComp and
pushforwardCongr. Transport along overFunctorEquiv, which is the identification
used to define schemeOpenModuleAdjunction and schemeMVUnderivedOpenRestriction.
The equalities are natural in I and commute with its differentials. Apply the
termwise functors, then the homotopy quotient; the quotient counit formula
mapHomotopyCategory_counit_app_quotient identifies their counits. Every homotopy
object is a quotient of a complex, so this gives the displayed equation for all K.
For the empty open this is the unique map between zero objects; for the full open
it is the same sectionwise identity. No derived comparison occurs here.
